routes.description: Defend historicity by arguing that Paul treated Jesus as an earthly person and that kinship and later historical testimony preserve identifiable human connections.
routes.successCriteria: Show that the cited Pauline language and historical witnesses are better explained by an earthly Jesus with real relatives than by a wholly celestial origin.

motionBridge.description: The cumulative evidence supports Jesus having existed as an earthly historical person.

centralBridges.description: Paul's language about birth, Jewish status, death, and burial locates Jesus in human history.
Paul's description of James identifies a biological relative of Jesus rather than generic Christian kinship.
Non-Pauline historical testimony independently connects Christianity to an executed earthly founder.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Traditions about Jesus's relatives and their leadership preserve a traceable family dynasty.

routes.description: Defend the celestial-origin hypothesis by emphasizing ambiguity in Paul, dependence or lateness in later sources, and the absence of secure contemporary earthly attestation.
routes.successCriteria: Show that the evidence cited for historicity is ambiguous, dependent, or legendary and does not distinguish an earthly founder from a celestial Christ later historicized.

motionBridge.description: The surviving evidence does not establish an earthly Jesus over a celestial or mythic origin.

centralBridges.description: Paul's language is compatible with allegorical birth, revelatory knowledge, and celestial events.
Later historical references cannot be shown to derive from sources independent of Christian tradition.
Jesus resembles other suffering-savior figures whose placement in history does not establish existence.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Late family traditions are legendary developments rather than independent memories of biological relatives.

sections.title: Pauline Embodiment
sections.rationale: The interpretation of Paul's birth, legal status, death, and burial language directly affects whether his Christ is placed in earthly history.

sections.title: James and Kinship
sections.rationale: Whether James is a biological brother or a cultic brother is a central contested link between Paul and an earthly Jesus.

sections.title: Tacitus and Source Independence
sections.rationale: Tacitus matters only insofar as his information independently corroborates an executed founder rather than repeating Christian reports.

sections.title: Family Dynasty Tradition
sections.rationale: The Hegesippus material bears on whether later claims about Jesus's relatives preserve history or reflect developing legend.
